results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.

result.title: API Validation Rules - Updated Decision
result.content:
Decision: Updated API validation rules based on Q3 2024 incident learnings.

Previous Rule:
We validate all API inputs against a JSON schema. Empty arrays are rejected. Updated 2024-11-01.

Updated Rule (as of 2024-11-15):
1. Validate all API inputs against a JSON schema
2. Empty arrays are rejected unless explicitly documented in endpoint specification
3. Rate limit changes require 72-hour advance notice to clients
4. All API responses must include rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)
5. Clients must have a documented escalation path for rate limit concerns

Rationale:
The Q3 2024 rate limit incident revealed gaps in our API validation and communication strategy. This updated decision incorporates three critical lessons: advance notice requirements prevent client outages, rate limit headers provide transparency, and escalation paths ensure customer support. These changes reduce incident risk and improve API reliability.

Updated 2024-11-15
